---
title: "Examples"
---

Six complete workflows, each ported from a canonical, citable R original and
worked **backward from a realistic end model** — the model's requirements decide
the recipe. Every page executes at build time, so the outputs shown are real.

Each example links two views:

- **Report** — the shoez/sklearn version, run top to bottom with live output.
- **R ↔ Python** — the R original and the port side by side, line-matched, with
  differences and remaining shoez gaps annotated in the code.

**[Ames mini](ames-mini-lm.qmd)** — the simple intro · [R ↔ Py](sbs/tmwr01-r-vs-py.html){target="_blank"}
: Linear regression. Recipe: encode.

**[Ames realistic](ames-realistic-lm.qmd)** — the canonical lm recipe · [R ↔ Py](sbs/tmwr03-r-vs-py.html){target="_blank"}
: Linear regression. Recipe: encode, interactions\*, splines\*.

**[Ames + xgboost](ames-xgboost.qmd)** — the model flips the recipe · [R ↔ Py](sbs/tmwr11-r-vs-py.html){target="_blank"}
: Gradient boosting, tuned. Recipe: one-hot, zero-variance filter.

**[Concrete + KNN](concrete-knn.qmd)** — scale is the admission ticket · [R ↔ Py](sbs/tmwr14-r-vs-py.html){target="_blank"}
: K-nearest neighbors, tuned. Recipe: normalize.

**[Beans PCA](beans-pca.qmd)** — a recipe with no model · [R ↔ Py](sbs/tmwr16-r-vs-py.html){target="_blank"}
: No estimator — the recipe is the product. Recipe: zero-variance filter, normalize, PCA.

**[Credit + glmnet](credit-glmnet.qmd)** — the imputation example · [R ↔ Py](sbs/kuhn-r-vs-py.html){target="_blank"}
: Regularized logistic, tuned. Recipe: impute, encode, filter, normalize.

\* marked steps are not yet built in shoez; the reports run the buildable subset
and the side-by-sides mark each gap in red where it occurs.

The two Ames rows are deliberately a pair: same data, same predictors, different
model — and the recipe transforms accordingly. There is also a
[side-by-side index](sbs/sbs-index.html){target="_blank"} listing all six
comparisons with their run results.

## Running the examples locally

The reports execute with the `examples` extra:

```bash
uv sync --extra examples
uv run quarto render examples   # or: great-docs build
```

Datasets are vendored under `examples/data/` as parquet (exported from R's
[modeldata](https://modeldata.tidymodels.org/) package: `ames`, `concrete`,
`credit_data`, and the dry-beans data from Koklu & Ozkan via the
[beans](https://github.com/tidymodels/beans) package).
